title: A finite infinitesimal Fitting bound detects a smooth generic fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], put $R=k[[t]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(t^n))$ for $n\geq1$. Let $f:Y\to S$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented morphism [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose its special fibre $X=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is Cohen-Macaulay, meaning $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ at every point [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and is equidimensional of dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Write $X_n=Y\times_S S_n$. If for some $n\geq1$ the image of $t^{n-1}$ is a global section of $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{X_n/S_n})\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_n}$ [def-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], then $Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k((t))$ is smooth over $k((t))$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

proof.text: For an open U containing the special fibre, the proper image of its closed complement is closed. Any nonempty closed subset of Spec k[[t]] contains its closed point, since every point specializes to the maximal ideal. Pullback point-surjectivity would then give a special-fibre point outside U, a contradiction. Hence U=Y. This uses only the local-ring structure of power series, not regularity or a classification of its primes. The quotient constant-coefficient map induces an isomorphism between the stated special fibre and the residue-field fibre over the closed point; its residue map is an isomorphism because it is a surjective map of fields.

Apply [lem-sbc-fibre-cohen-macaulay-locus-open]. The special-fibre isomorphism transports depth using the existing private depth_eq_of_ringEquiv helper from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.FibreCohenMacaulayLocus (import all), and transports ring Krull dimension by stalk ring isomorphisms, so this open contains the special fibre and is all of Y by step 1. Apply [lem-sbc-cohen-macaulay-fibre-dimension-decomposition] with both opens top. By [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] and local finite type of the special fibre, its local topological dimension is d. The partition piece of dimension d contains every special-fibre point, hence is Y by step 1. Thus every fibre has local dimension d.

Identify differential sections on affine charts using [lem-sc-relative-differentials-affine-sections]; they are finite modules by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Choose a finite free surjection and apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally] to calculate the sheaf ideal. The tensor differential equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], together with [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], proves the affine Fitting base-change formula. Apply it to the closed jet immersion. Its kernel on an affine chart is generated by t^n, by the quotient kernel formula and [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension]. The global jet section restricts into the extended Fitting ideal, so surjectivity on sections gives b in the original Fitting ideal and a with t^(n-1)=b+t^n a.

On each affine chart take the basic open D(1-ta) for its a from step 3. At a special-fibre point t is a nonunit in the local ring, so 1-ta is a unit. The union contains the special fibre and is all of Y by step 1. On the Laurent-series generic fibre t is invertible, since k((t)) is the localization of k[[t]] at t. The identity (1-ta)t^(n-1)=b thus makes b a unit in each generic-fibre stalk lying over that basic open. Such a point is outside the Fitting support. This applies without cancellation by t and includes n=1.

By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally], each generic-fibre image point has d generators for its differential stalk. Flatness and the dimension equality of step 2 make [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-differential-criterion] applicable, yielding a smooth open neighbourhood in Y. Pull these opens back to the generic fibre. Its base map is an open immersion, so its first projection is also an open immersion. Restrict each smooth neighbourhood along this projection, cancel the monomorphism from Spec k((t)) to the base using stability of smoothness under base change, and apply Mathlib Zariski source locality. The pulled-back opens cover, including when the source is empty.
